title: Restore the input group for Voxtype evdev hotkey users
head: 1c88d0536922
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Removing Voxtype leaves behind the migration's persistent input-group grant
leads.consequence: On an account granted input by this migration, omarchy-voxtype-remove removes the package and ~/.config/voxtype but does not drop input membership. The account retains read/write access to /dev/input/event* for all its programs after logout and login, although the opt-in feature is gone. Neither the packaged voxtype-bin post_remove hook (which only deletes symlinks) nor the Omarchy remover revokes input; the earlier removal migration 1787865477 is already marked complete by omarchy-migrate:91-96 and does not run again. Do not remove membership indiscriminately: an account may also use ydotool or have a separately administered grant. Track provenance or provide a safe opt-out and explain the manual removal path.
leads.triage: factually confirmed (bin/omarchy-voxtype-remove:10-24 does not touch groups; voxtype-bin post_remove only removes binaries); not published: lifecycle gap outside the migration's repair scope, and a blanket removal would be wrong

leads.summary: One-time predicate cannot grant input to users who opt into Voxtype after the migration
leads.consequence: The new test checks a user who already has enabled=true when the migration runs, but normal Omarchy installation copies enabled=false. Fresh installs pre-mark this migration before the optional Voxtype install; existing users with disabled Voxtype also acquire the marker after the migration no-ops. If either later sets enabled=true, omarchy-migrate skips the completed migration, so the evdev hotkey still lacks input-group access. The related #7302 instruction to enable the built-in hotkey is affected. The voxtype-bin post_install message does mention a manual `sudo usermod -aG input $USER`, but neither Omarchy's end-user dictation manual nor the config-changing flow connects that instruction to a later opt-in. Offer a deliberate grant path when changing the hotkey setting or document this manual command at the point of opt-in; a one-shot migration alone only repairs already-opted-in existing users.
leads.triage: factually confirmed (omarchy-provision-user pre-marks; install copies enabled=false); matches Opus H3; not published: pre-existing, outside PR scope

leads.summary: Voxtype salvage can turn an explicitly disabled but malformed hotkey section into a privileged grant
leads.consequence: For valid TOML with `[hotkey] enabled = false` and a wrongly typed sibling such as `key = 7`, Voxtype 1.1.0 rejects the whole hotkey section, substitutes its built-in enabled=true, and `config get hotkey.enabled` prints true. The migration then grants persistent input membership despite an explicit enabled=false; RUST_LOG=off suppresses the warning about the rejected section. This matches the daemon's salvaged setting, but not the user's expressed opt-in. If the guard is intended to enforce explicit opt-in for this security-sensitive group, validate that the literal file setting was explicitly true (or reject a salvaged section) before granting; keep environment-only opt-ins an explicit policy decision.
leads.triage: behavioural; sent to Opus (followup-1.md), confirmed in sandbox plan-g on 1.1.0 and 1.1.1-rc4; published in Details under the design point

leads.summary: Migration test cannot detect a recurrence of the stdout-log regression
leads.consequence: The mock Voxtype never emits trace/warning lines and does not inspect RUST_LOG. Removing the newly added RUST_LOG=off prefix from the migration leaves every existing test case unchanged, while a real Voxtype 1.1.0 with a salvaged config section and inherited RUST_LOG=debug emits a warning before the true value. Extend the stub so it emits a log line before true unless RUST_LOG=off, then assert the grant and reboot marker for that case. The existing nonzero-exit test remains useful for the fail-open comparison mutant; it does not exercise the logging fix.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2; published as Optional test improvement

limits: I01-I03 were traced from pinned Omarchy and tagged Voxtype 1.1.0 sources, not executed against a native Voxtype binary. Upstream source is sufficient for the stated paths, but an executable reproduction would add confidence. Other open PRs were inspected by diff for the relevant feature paths; combined merged-code test suites were not run, so no claim of successful combined test runs is made.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** One minor new issue: the acceptance security check still rejects the `input` membership this migration grants.

[Earlier findings](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12015#issuecomment-5860769600) at `1c88d053`: stdout log lines, the fail-open test gap and the Hyprland comment are resolved. The `$USER` target and the user-writable gate are unchanged.

### Acceptance security check rejects the restored group

`verify_input_group` in `test/acceptance.d/security-test.sh` allows `input` only with `xpadneo-dkms` or `ydotool` installed. **Impact:** where this migration restored `input` and neither package is installed, the check fails with `not ok - user is not in the input group`. Acceptance VMs lack Voxtype by default.

**Suggested change:** also accept `[[ $(RUST_LOG=off voxtype config get hotkey.enabled 2>/dev/null) == "true" ]]` there and update its comment.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 1c88d053)</summary>

Self-contained script, run from an Omarchy checkout (`bash acceptance-input-group-case.sh .`). Everything is stubbed: `id` and `gpasswd` share a fake group list, `pacman` knows no packages, `sudo -n` fails, `grim` does nothing. No real groups, sudo or accounts are touched.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

root=${1:?omarchy checkout}
test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_dir"' EXIT

stub_bin="$test_dir/bin"
mkdir -p "$stub_bin"
printf 'wheel\n' >"$test_dir/groups"

cat >"$stub_bin/id" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
[[ ${1:-} == "-nG" ]] || exit 2
cat "$STUB_GROUPS_FILE"
STUB
cat >"$stub_bin/gpasswd" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
[[ $1 == "-a" ]] || exit 2
printf '%s %s\n' "$(cat "$STUB_GROUPS_FILE")" "$3" >"$STUB_GROUPS_FILE"
STUB
cat >"$stub_bin/sudo" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
[[ ${1:-} == "-n" ]] && exit 1
exec "$@"
STUB
cat >"$stub_bin/pacman" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
exit 1
STUB
cat >"$stub_bin/omarchy-cmd-present" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
exit 0
STUB
cat >"$stub_bin/voxtype" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
[[ $1 == "config" && $2 == "get" && $3 == "hotkey.enabled" ]] || exit 2
printf 'true\n'
STUB
cat >"$stub_bin/omarchy-state" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
exit 0
STUB
cat >"$stub_bin/grim" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
exit 0
STUB
chmod +x "$stub_bin"/*

export STUB_GROUPS_FILE="$test_dir/groups"

echo "== migrations/1789490499.sh (hotkey enabled, no xpadneo-dkms, no ydotool)"
USER=tester PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" bash -euo pipefail "$root/migrations/1789490499.sh"
echo "groups now: $(cat "$STUB_GROUPS_FILE")"

echo "== test/acceptance.d/security-test.sh"
set +e
OMARCHY_ACCEPTANCE_DIR="$test_dir/artifacts" PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" \
  bash "$root/test/acceptance.d/security-test.sh"
status=$?
set -e
echo "acceptance security-test exit status: $status"
```

Actual output at 1c88d053 (stdout, then stderr):

```text
== migrations/1789490499.sh (hotkey enabled, no xpadneo-dkms, no ydotool)
Restore the input group for users who opted into Voxtype's evdev hotkey
Restored tester to the input group for the Voxtype hotkey. Log out and back in to apply.
groups now: wheel input
== test/acceptance.d/security-test.sh
acceptance security-test exit status: 1
```

```text
no controller or ydotool support installed to justify it
not ok - user is not in the input group
```

The same output was produced with the PR's two files applied on top of current `quattro`.

With the suggested change to `verify_input_group`, the same script prints:

```text
== migrations/1789490499.sh (hotkey enabled, no xpadneo-dkms, no ydotool)
Restore the input group for users who opted into Voxtype's evdev hotkey
Restored tester to the input group for the Voxtype hotkey. Log out and back in to apply.
groups now: wheel input
== test/acceptance.d/security-test.sh
ok - input group membership is backed by an opt-in feature
ok - asdcontrol sudoers check skipped: sudo needs a password
ok - sshd hardening exercise skipped: set OMARCHY_ACCEPTANCE_SUDO_PASSWORD to run it
acceptance security-test exit status: 0
```

Suggested change used for that run:

```diff
--- a/test/acceptance.d/security-test.sh
+++ b/test/acceptance.d/security-test.sh
@@ -15,11 +15,12 @@
 source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
 
 # Membership of `input` gives raw access to /dev/input/event*: any process
-# running as the user could log keystrokes. Only the opt-in controller and
-# ydotool features may grant it.
+# running as the user could log keystrokes. Only the opt-in controller, ydotool
+# and Voxtype evdev hotkey features may grant it.
 verify_input_group() {
   if id -nG | grep -qw input; then
-    if pacman -Q xpadneo-dkms &>/dev/null || pacman -Q ydotool &>/dev/null; then
+    if pacman -Q xpadneo-dkms &>/dev/null || pacman -Q ydotool &>/dev/null ||
+      [[ $(RUST_LOG=off voxtype config get hotkey.enabled 2>/dev/null) == "true" ]]; then
       pass "input group membership is backed by an opt-in feature"
     else
       fail "user is not in the input group" "no controller or ydotool support installed to justify it"
```
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified at 1c88d053:**
- `RUST_LOG=off voxtype config get hotkey.enabled` printed exactly `true`, `false` or nothing in all 90 sandbox runs across Voxtype 1.0.1, 1.1.0 (the packaged version) and 1.1.1-rc4, with `RUST_LOG` unset, `debug` or `trace`. The old form failed the check in 43 runs whose value was `true`. It also silences a new stdout warning that 1.1.1-rc4 prints for a misplaced config section.
- The real `omarchy-migrate` (with stubbed `id`, `sudo`, `gpasswd`, `pacman` and `omarchy-state`) restores `input` at 1c88d053 with `RUST_LOG=debug` or `RUST_LOG=trace`, including `trace` combined with a bad `[audio]` value. That combined setup at d1943054 does not.
- The new fail-closed case fails against a `!= "false"` mutant, and the PR test passes 5 of 5 at the head.
- The out-of-order timestamp is fine: `omarchy-migrate` runs every unmarked migration, and fresh installs pre-mark all of them.

**Design point, new detail:** on Voxtype 1.1.0 and 1.1.1-rc4, a wrongly typed value in `[hotkey]` (for example `key = 7` next to `enabled = false`, or a quoted `enabled = "false"`) makes Voxtype drop the whole section and use the built-in default. `config get` then prints `true`, and the migration grants `input`. The daemon does run the built-in Scroll Lock evdev hotkey in that case, but the user wrote the hotkey off. On 1.0.1 the whole file is rejected and the migration skips.

**Unchanged:** the `$USER` point (open #8534 still covers only `bin/` commands). Voxtype before 1.0 has no `config get`, which needs no action because packages are upgraded before migrations run and Omarchy ships Voxtype 1.1.0.
</details>

<details><summary>Optional notes</summary>

**Optional test improvement:** the PR test passes even with `RUST_LOG=off` removed, because the `voxtype` stub never prints a log line. The case below fails with the d1943054 migration and passes at 1c88d053:

```diff
--- a/test/shell.d/voxtype-input-group-migration-test.sh
+++ b/test/shell.d/voxtype-input-group-migration-test.sh
@@ -23,6 +23,8 @@
 #!/bin/bash
 [[ $1 == "config" && $2 == "get" && $3 == "hotkey.enabled" ]] || exit 2
 [[ ${STUB_VOXTYPE_FAILS:-0} == "0" ]] || exit 1
+# Voxtype writes its tracing output to stdout, and RUST_LOG overrides its level.
+[[ ${RUST_LOG:-off} == "off" ]] || printf '%s\n' ' DEBUG Loading config from "/home/tester/.config/voxtype/config.toml"'
 printf '%s\n' "${STUB_HOTKEY_ENABLED:-false}"
 STUB
 cat >"$stub_bin/sudo" <<'STUB'
@@ -73,3 +75,7 @@
 [[ ! -e $gpasswd_calls ]] || fail "migration does not grant input when voxtype config get fails"
 [[ ! -e $state_calls ]] || fail "a failed voxtype query does not flag a reboot"
 pass "migration fails closed when the Voxtype config query fails"
+
+RUST_LOG=debug run_migration "wheel" true >/dev/null
+grep -qsxF -- "-a tester input" "$gpasswd_calls" || fail "migration restores input when RUST_LOG is set in the update environment"
+pass "migration ignores Voxtype log output when reading hotkey.enabled"
```

With the migration from d1943054, the new case prints `not ok - migration restores input when RUST_LOG is set in the update environment`.
</details>
